verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents running the complete platform on your own infrastructure for data sovereignty, with Docker and Kubernetes/Helm deployment guides and a self-hosted Edge Proxy that evaluates flags close to your servers. The public GitHub repo serves as the distribution, and a community evaluator tested Flagsmith among self-hosted tools, though they found it less polished. missing for 10: no explicit open-source license statement in the evidence, no documentation of feature parity between self-hosted and SaaS editions.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can self-host the full flag platform from an open-source distribution, keeping evaluation data on my infrastructure

citations.quote: Self-hosting Flagsmith allows you to run the complete Flagsmith platform within your own infrastructure, giving you full control over your data, security policies, and deployment environment.
**Data sovereignty**: Keep your feature flag data within your own infrastructure
Kubernetes and OpenShift: Full Kubernetes deployment with Helm charts and operators
Run the Edge Proxy within in your own infrastructure and connect to it from your server-side SDKs
This guide explains how to run a full Flagsmith environment on your local machine using Docker.
